candidates.title: Coca-Cola didn't invent the red Santa; 33 years of repeating Sundblom's Santa made the world credit it
candidates.event_date: Sundblom ads 1931-1964; spark: Coca-Cola Holiday Caravan announced 2026-11-11

sources.claim: 'Coca-Cola did not create the legend of Santa Claus' but its advertising 'did play a big role in shaping' him; commissioned Haddon Sundblom in 1931

Red outfits existed before Coca-Cola's campaign; Sundblom's Santa ran in Coca-Cola ads 1931-1964 in Saturday Evening Post, National Geographic, The New Yorker etc., and on billboards, calendars, store displays
Verdict false: red-suited Santa existed since at least the 19th century (e.g. 1868 'Sugar Plums' confectionery ad; Nast 1881)
White Rock used the modern Santa in ads in 1915 and 1923; Coca-Cola led the popularisation through repetition
White Rock ran Santa ads in 1915-16 (b/w) and colour ads in 1923-25 'indistinguishable from Coke's 1930' ads
Moore's 1823 poem never mentions red; Nast's drawings (Merry Old Santa Claus, Harper's Weekly, 1 Jan 1881) credited with the red coat
Coca-Cola Holiday Caravan returns across North America; 'share a Coke with Santa' at stops (seasonal spark only)

candidates.claim: The myth that Coca-Cola dressed Santa in its brand red is one of the most shared brand 'facts'; the truth (red Santa predates 1931; Coke owned him by repeating him for 33 years) is a surprising, verifiable reversal.
candidates.evidence_of_virality: Evergreen myth: fact-checked by at least four outlets (Ferret, Logically, VERIFY/KGW, The Hustle) and answered on Coca-Cola's own FAQ pages in several countries (US, GB, IE, PK, PL, AT seen in search) = recurring public curiosity every December (estimate, no search-volume data pulled). Seasonal relevance: Christmas ad season and Holiday Caravan (2026-11-11).
candidates.scores_are_estimates: trend_virality, curiosity, story and lesson are editorial estimates; not measured

lenses.red_team: Do not say Coca-Cola 'chose red to match its logo' (unsupported) or that Coke 'had nothing to do with it' (also wrong: it shaped the face and popularised the image). Safe claim: red Santas existed decades before 1931; Coca-Cola didn't invent him; its ads repeated one Santa every year 1931-1964, and now the world credits Coke. Avoid citing exact earliest-year 'firsts' on screen; use 'decades before'. Coca-Cola appeared as a nuance in 2026-11-08 (AI ad); today's angle (ownership through repetition) is different.
lenses.audience_psychology: 'Everything you knew is wrong' about a childhood icon + a giant brand = high share/save impulse; viewer feels smart sharing it. Persian audience knows Baba Noel and Coca-Cola; international audience entering Christmas season.
lenses.brand_fit: Pure brand strategy: distinctive assets, consistency, owning a moment/colour, 'you don't need to be first, you need to be consistent'. Fits Behnood's strategist voice; usable lesson for small business owners.
